clue.text: Non-PC gay getting some stick

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an offensive slang term for a gay man
second meaning: a bundle of sticks tied together for firewood

explanation.surface: A gay man is on the receiving end of homophobic abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting some stick' reads as being abused; here 'some stick' is a bundle of firewood, the word's original sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a homophobic slur and an old term for a bound bundle of firewood sticks.

clue.text: Second nature to put topless, backless bodice on oneself?

indicators.note: topless means losing its top, so the opening letter of the garment's name goes; backless describes the garment itself

parts.note: a halter is a top held by a neck strap, leaving the back bare
the ego is the self

explanation.surface: Stripping off a revealing top comes naturally to someone, it suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: A halter top is held up by a neck strap and leaves the back bare, so 'backless' describes the garment rather than signalling a second cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self or other personality, which the clue renders loosely as a second nature.

clue.text: Meanness defines a princess

indicators.note: the word read as de-fines, giving boundaries, so the outer word marks out the limits of the run of letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the middle of this word

explanation.surface: Royal stinginess is the defining trait of one of the Queen's children.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Anne, the Princess Royal, is the Queen's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is the name of a British princess, the Princess Royal, so the answer is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Tranquillity, right, is not commonly shown by hard line Islamic protestors? No

definitions.text: shown by hard line Islamic protestors? No

parts.note: rest is peace and quiet
R is the usual abbreviation for right
ain't is the colloquial form of is not

explanation.surface: A jibe that hardline Islamist demonstrators never show calm, propriety or self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole closing statement: the quality that hardline protestors, the setter suggests, do not show.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control and moderation, the opposite of the violent excess the clue attributes to hardline protestors.

clue.text: Leader of Conservatives dogged by stink — could get fed to the dogs

definitions.text: could get fed to the dogs

indicators.note: the leader of a group is its front, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the party name
a hum is a bad smell in British slang

explanation.surface: The Tory leader, followed by a whiff of scandal, might be thrown to the dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged by' puts the smell after the leader. Chum is also a well-known British brand of dog food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chum is chopped bait or scraps, and as a British dog-food brand name it is literally food given to dogs.

clue.text: You know what you can do — ski off piste, centrally, I say, to get behind

definitions.text: You know what you can do

indicators.note: skiing off piste means going off the groomed route, so the letters stray out of order

parts.note: the three letters rearranged

indicators.note: centrally points to the middle of the word, so only its central letter is used

parts.note: the middle letter of the five
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise like 'I say!'
British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal from a skier who has gone off piste, telling someone to follow behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off piste' looks like part of the skiing picture but rearranges ski; arse is British slang for bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: 'You know what you can do' is a polite stand-in for an insulting brush-off, and this rude phrase is exactly such a dismissal.

clue.text: Shrink has soldiers put on contraceptive device

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
a coil is an intrauterine contraceptive

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist arranges for troops to be issued with contraception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' poses as the slang noun for a psychiatrist; it is the verb meaning to draw back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to flinch away in fear or disgust, which is one sense of the verb shrink.

clue.text: Filthy beast's extra large sheet removed for safety reasons?

indicators.note: something filthy has been messed up, so the letters that follow are muddled

parts.note: the possessive taken as the plain letters
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: A dirty animal's oversized bedsheet has been taken away for hygiene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheet' suggests bedding; it is asbestos sheeting, stripped from old buildings because the fibres are a health risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos came in sheets as building material and is now removed because its fibres cause lung disease.

clue.text: Ex-president, complete arse to Spain

parts.note: all means entire or complete
the rear end, slang for the backside
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A former head of state is insulted as an utter fool in Spanish eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Salvador Allende was the president of Chile overthrown in 1973. 'Complete arse' reads as an insult but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Allende was president of Chile until the 1973 coup, so he is a former head of state.

clue.text: He rises, excited for Paris, perhaps

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and jump about, so they land in a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man becomes aroused by the French capital, or by a famous socialite.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is not the city: it is Paris Hilton, heir to the hotel fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris Hilton is an example of a woman who will inherit a great fortune.

clue.text: Cripes! Boris finally gets English birds

parts.note: both are mild exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the name is used

parts.note: the closing letter of the name
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson exclaims in surprise at last winning over some English girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birds' plays on British slang for young women, but here it means actual birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Geese are large waterfowl, so they are an example of birds.

clue.text: A monument to Martin Bell's entrances, almost pissed

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter of the slang word is cut

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an entrance is the way in, so the opening letters of the two names are taken

parts.note: the opening letter of each name
stoned means drunk or high

explanation.surface: A memorial to the anti-sleaze MP Martin Bell, who arrives very drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin Bell was a BBC war reporter who became an independent MP. Pissed is British slang for drunk, and STONED loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombstone is a stone memorial set over a grave, a kind of monument.

clue.text: (& 19ac.) Brenda's lot, maritally? Hey! screwing around with Foreign Office

indicators.note: screwing around suggests messing about wildly, so the letters are thoroughly jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office

explanation.surface: Gossip about royal infidelity and the diplomats who get involved with the royals.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen. 'Maritally' looks like part of the definition but is all anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda being the Queen, her lot means her relatives, the British monarch's household.

clue.text: A closet gay no longer holds student group to be markedly inferior

indicators.note: something that holds another keeps it inside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a gay person no longer in the closet has been outed
a class is a group of students

explanation.surface: A man who has come out joins a student society and is looked down on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closet' sets up a secret, but the whole phrase means someone whose sexuality is now public.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outclassed is to be clearly beaten by a superior rival, so plainly inferior.

clue.text: Regard Grant's small organ?

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
the apostrophe-s stands for 'is': grant is let, as in allow

explanation.surface: Someone is told to consider Hugh Grant's modest endowment.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant looks like the actor's name; it is the verb to allow. The question mark flags that the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole, and its name means a little eye, so it is jokily a tiny version of an organ.

clue.text: Kinky Nurse Cold Arse

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent out of their order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about a pervy, frigid nurse's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Arse looks like the body part; in British slang it also means a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: An arse in British slang is an obnoxious, worthless person, which is what a villain or rogue is.

clue.text: Bush shows what's needed to take down a dictator — Henry goes "Sonofabitch is telling porkies!"

indicators.note: a person who goes leaves, so the letter standing for that name departs from the word

parts.words: what's needed to take down a dictator
parts.note: the quick writing system a secretary uses to record dictation
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
a cur is a contemptible man, and literally a dog born of a bitch
porkies, from pork pies, is rhyming slang for lies

explanation.surface: President Bush learns what it takes to topple a tyrant, while someone named Henry calls him a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush is not the president but pubic hair; 'dictator' is someone dictating letters, not a tyrant. SHORTHAND drops its H.
explanation.definitionFit: The short and curlies is British slang for pubic hair, which is also called the bush.

clue.text: Failing to get an erection with fruity bit, but not blatant about it?

parts.note: not hard
the core is the central part of a fruit such as an apple

explanation.surface: A man who cannot rise to the occasion is coy about his saucy sideline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' hints at smut, but here it is plain fruit. 'It' is sex, so the definition means sexually suggestive without being explicit.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-core pornography implies sex rather than showing it explicitly, so it is restrained about it.

clue.text: "Suggestive" Independent writer "dead" — ousted by Charles's no. 1

indicators.note: to be ousted is to be thrown out and replaced, so one letter takes another's place
the writer being dead means that author is gone from the newspaper's name

parts.note: the British newspaper's name, taken as written
a pen is a writing tool
the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style story about a suggestive columnist on The Independent dying and being replaced by Prince Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing PEN leaves INDEDENT; 'dead' also stands for D (the abbreviation in obituaries), and C ousts the second D.
explanation.definitionFit: Suggestive can mean hinting at sex, and indecent describes material that is sexually improper.

clue.text: (see 13ac.)
Communist article accepted by "wet"

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the small word goes inside the other

parts.note: damp, slightly wet
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A hard-line Communist dismisses a moderate as a wet.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a 'wet' is a moderate Conservative; here it just means damp.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Mao Zedong's version of revolutionary politics is a kind of communist.

clue.text: Little sweet butt, er, Fanny, etc.?

definitions.note: the answer is singular; 'etc.' widens the example to the general term

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a dessert
the butt end of something is its end
both are sounds of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone praises a cute bottom and stumbles over a rude word for a woman's privates.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanny is British slang for the female genitals, not the American backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The pudendum is the external genitals, and fanny is British slang for the female ones.

clue.text: Cyclops Award presented to King Dick

parts.note: Cyclops is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter refers to himself
a British honour given in the New Year and Birthday lists
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The magazine's own prize is handed to a king who is an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for 'me'. Dick is not an insult here but slang for the male organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Member is a euphemism for the penis, and dick is slang for the same thing.

clue.text: Sod what you're doing!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an angry word, i.e. a swear word, which sod is
second meaning: the puzzle the solver is working on right now

explanation.surface: An exasperated person swears at whatever someone is busy with.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as two words, cross and word: sod is an angry word. Sod is a mild British expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sod is literally a cross (angry) word, and the solver is in the middle of doing one of these puzzles.

clue.text: Get them, Roger!

parts.note: surface reading: an order to a man called Roger to fetch something
setter's reading: to roger is British slang for having sex, and 'getting one's ___' is an idiom for the same

explanation.walkthrough: Roger looks like a name or radio 'received'; here it is the slang verb for sex, matching the idiom about getting a man's share of sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to get one's oats' means to have sex, which is what roger means as a slang verb.

clue.text: See copper pressed against male member of clergy?

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A policeman pushed up against a male priest, with a hint of scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' suggests a bishop's diocese and 'copper' a policeman; neither is. The question mark marks the definition as an example: a locum is any stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a temporary stand-in for a professional, such as a priest covering another's parish.

clue.text: Time to leave coffee, having become stiff

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so that letter is taken out of the drink

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Coffee left too long has gone cold and solid.
explanation.walkthrough: A stiff is slang for a corpse, so 'having become stiff' means having died.
explanation.definitionFit: Late means dead, as in 'the late king', and a body that has died goes stiff.

clue.text: Brenda's back on speed, pussy possibly concealing cocaine (as the street-wise admirer says)

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the royal abbreviation is read from its end

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina; Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen
s is the symbol for speed in physics

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so the pet wraps around the drug

parts.note: a pussy cat is an example of a pet
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled scene involving the Queen, amphetamines and cocaine hidden in a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Speed and cocaine sit in a drugs picture, but speed is a symbol and cocaine a single letter. The definition is the street greeting itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In street slang a single word of approval like this means admiration for someone's achievement or style.

clue.text: Government enterprise stifles political understanding

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother or hold in, so the phrase keeps the letters hidden inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A state-run business is accused of suppressing political agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of the first word and the start of the second carry the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale between Britain and France.
